Build the enforcement for the `childEnv()` convention (a check over `packages/cli/test/**` refusing bare `{ ...process.env` in spawner files, with the same carve-out discipline the choke point documents). **Family note (fold-or-serial is a required answer at dispatch)**: #11441 (worklist two files short — one spawns a real `os serve`) and #11464 (bin/run.js + ts-path NODE_ENV pair silently cancels) are the same test-spawner-hygiene family; five-gate test says same package, same defect class — a fold into one dispatch is plausible and the cli seat answers it explicitly.

## Claim — `domain:cli` seat

Session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`, branch `claude/issue-11341-childenv-spawner-gate`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` + assignee in one stroke, read back.

### fold-or-serial — the required answer, per gate

Triage (`5389800919`) named this explicitly: #11341 / #11441 / #11464 are the same test-spawner-hygiene family and *"the cli seat answers it explicitly."* Answering:

| card | gate ① — same defect form AND same fix? | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **#11441** (worklist two files short, one spawns a real `os serve`) | **Yes.** It reports that #11341's hand-built worklist missed two files in the same population, with the same remedy. | **Absorbed by construction** — see below. ⛔ Not folded as a card (it is an ungraded `finding`; grading is triage's). |
| **#11464** (`bin/run.js` + a ts-path-enabling `NODE_ENV` silently cancel) | **No.** Different defect: not an env leak into the child, but two child-env settings cancelling each other. And its **guard's polarity depends on the #11317 ruling**, which is with the maintainer — it carries `Blocked-by: #11317`. | ⛔ **Not folded, not serial-behind-this — blocked upstream.** |

⭐ **#11441 needs no fold because a gate has no worklist.** #11341's deliverable is enforcement over `packages/cli/test/**`; the two files #11441 names are *members of that population*, not extra scope. A gate that needed a hand-maintained file list would be the same defect one level up. Covering them is the gate working, not the card widening. Say in your report whether the population you enumerate contains them.

**Declared file surface**: the new check script (under `scripts/`, following this repo's existing check conventions) plus its self-test and its wiring into the gate set. Plus a baseline file if you use one — see the fence.

### ⛔ Hard fence: gate + shrink-only baseline. Do NOT fix the existing violations.

Measured just now on `origin/main`: **at least ten files** under `packages/cli/test/**` carry a bare `{ ...process.env` — including `generate-skill.e2e.test.ts` and `generate-agent-retired.e2e.test.ts`.

**Those two belong to in-flight #11071's neighbourhood** (the generator card, dispatched to a parallel dev this same round). Editing them here would collide on the same files. So:

- ✅ Land the check and record today's violations in a **shrink-only baseline**, the ratchet shape this repo uses everywhere (`check:slot-lookup`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:where-matcher` are all live examples — read one before writing yours).
- ⛔ **Do not repair any existing violating file in this PR.** Burning the baseline down is follow-up work, one card per neighbourhood, after the ratchet exists.
- This is also what triage meant by *"with the same carve-out discipline the choke point documents"* — read that choke point and match it rather than inventing a carve-out syntax.

### What the gate must actually catch

The convention is `childEnv()`; the defect is a spawner reaching for `{ ...process.env }` directly and inheriting whatever the parent had — which is how `TEST=true` and `NODE_ENV` have twice leaked into children and produced false greens in this package (#11267, #11317).

⚠️ **Precision matters more than reach here.** A gate that flags every `...process.env` in the package will flag non-spawner uses and get carved out into uselessness. Scope it to spawner sites, and state in your report how you defined "spawner" and what your definition's false-positive and false-negative edges are. A self-test with a positive control (a fixture that SHOULD trip it) and a negative control (a legitimate use that must not) is the deliverable's real proof — `check:nul-bytes` and `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` are the house pattern.

### Anti-vacuity, for a gate

The pin is the self-test, and it must be shown failing: feed it a fixture with a bare spread and watch it exit non-zero; feed it the `childEnv()` form and watch it pass. ⛔ A gate whose self-test cannot fail is a gate that measures nothing — this repo has caught that shape before.

`Clause-②: no` expected — a new gate **tightens**; it moves no accept set and no public surface. (⛔ Note the asymmetry: *weakening* a gate is on the manual floor. Adding one is not.)

### Delivery

Changeset if anything published changes (a `scripts/` gate usually does not — say so and why if you skip it). Push, open a **draft** PR with `Fixes #11341`, derive the gate set with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, and quote each gate's own verdict line. **A gate that refuses is NOT MEASURED.**

## ACCEPT — armed

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`. PR **#11599** @ `acf5f14e`. Labels re-read before asserting: `tests` · `pm:dispatched` · `domain:cli`, no gate label — `Clause-②: no` holds (a new gate **tightens**; nothing widens).

**CI**: 34 check runs in one `perPage: 40`, all `completed` `success`/`skipped`. ⚠️ An earlier read at 07:4x caught `Lint & Repo Gates` still `in_progress` — `in_progress` is not `success`, so arming waited for it to finish rather than reading the aggregate as green.

### ⭐ The check this card needed that no other card does: proving the gate actually RUNS

A new gate's headline failure mode is being wired in but never executed — the job goes green because nothing ran. A green `Lint & Repo Gates` does not distinguish those two worlds, so it was verified from the workflow diff instead:

```yaml
- name: CLI test child-env guard
  run: pnpm check:cli-test-child-env
```

**No `if:` condition**, same level as its neighbours, in a job whose shell is `bash -e` — so a non-zero exit from either leg (`--self-test`, then the real scan) fails the step and reds the job. The job is `completed: success`. ⇒ **it ran, and both legs exited 0.**

⭐ The dev anticipated this exact concern in the workflow comment, unprompted: *"this gate computes its own population, so a scan that stopped matching would print a confident green over a tree it never read (#4690's family)"* — and put the self-test first as the structural answer, not as decoration.

### What was reviewed beyond green

**The fence held.** Five files changed; **not one** is a `packages/cli/test/**` violator. `generate-skill.e2e.test.ts` and `generate-agent-retired.e2e.test.ts` are baselined and untouched, as the #11071 hard-serial fence required.

**Two labels that looked alarming, both benign on inspection** — `size/xl` is the 909-line gate itself; `dependencies` is Auto Label reacting to `package.json` being touched, and that touch is **one npm-script line** in the house `--self-test && <real run>` form. ⛔ Not a new runtime dependency, so the manual floor is not in play.

**The remedy-authority edit is a registration, not a loosening.** `check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` gains a `CONTROL` entry declaring `expect: 'refused'`. ⭐ Better than that: the dev reports *"the sweep classified it that way on its own before the entry was written"* — the entry describes measured behaviour rather than asserting it.

**The definition was the deliverable, and it arrived with its edges.** *Spawner* = the file imports a process-creating API from `node:child_process` (named, namespace **or** default) or `Worker` from `node:worker_threads`. *Bulk* = `process.env` used as a whole value; reading one variable (`process.env.HOME`) is never flagged, and an assignment **target** (`process.env = saved`) is a write, not a copy — a rule narrowed mid-build with its own case after a self-test leg went red. Recall cost measured, not assumed: 82 sources, 28 spawners, **zero bulk references outside a spawner file**, so precision costs nothing today.

**Two registries, deliberately different kinds.** The shrink-only ratchet holds the 18 pre-existing leaks in 17 files. `DELIBERATE` is a *declaration*, pinned in **both** directions — so "cleaning up" #11267's pin leg (the one that proves the leak does something) now fails. That is the carve-out discipline the choke point documents, and it is the distinction that keeps a carve-out from decaying into a blanket exemption.

**Anti-vacuity, done to the standard the deliverable demands.** The self-test was **watched failing** — first run 4 of 53 red, both causes real (three fixtures hit the zero-spawners refusal; one mirror fixture held 2 refs, not 1), fixed, final 54 pass. The positive control runs **out of process** through the real `--audit-root` entry, on the stated ground that *"exits non-zero" cannot be observed from inside the process claiming it*. Four ablation legs cover four distinct failure shapes: a fresh violation, a second violation in an already-baselined file, a baseline entry gone stale, and a `DELIBERATE` pin "cleaned up".

⭐ **And the on-disk discipline caught a real no-op.** Leg 2's first `perl -0pi` anchor matched nothing and exited 0; the on-disk count read `1 → 1`, so it was **reported as NOT RUN and re-anchored** rather than quietly retried. That is precisely why "an editor's exit code proves nothing" is in every dispatch order on this lane — this is the first time this round it caught something.

`check:type-check-debt` refused first (a fresh-worktree property, not this diff), was reported as refused, then built to 70/70 and re-run to a real verdict. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` run **whole** — no narrowing claimed.

### Findings filed — ⛔ not this seat's to grade

- **#11595** — 8 spawner call sites pass **no `env` option at all**, so the child inherits the vitest worker environment verbatim. The same leak in a purer form, and the gate is deliberately silent on it: closing that is a decision about the `childEnv()` convention's **reach**, not about this defect. ⭐ Correct call — widening the gate to cover it would have smuggled a convention change in under a defect fix.
- **#11596** — burn down the baseline: 18 leaks / 17 files, split by neighbourhood, with the `serve-*` files flagged as needing the child re-checked after the strip (crypto-key persistence coupling) and `serve-app-anchored-optional-import` called out as the one that boots a real `os serve`.
